current.text: He is expected to start at center for Charlotte on opening night.
Charlotte has several centers who compete for his minutes: the rookie center taken 14th, Ryan Kalkbrenner and Steinbach. Grant Williams also plays some small-ball five.
The center plan is unclear. Coach Charles Lee is expected to try different frontcourt lineups, and closing lineups will change by matchup.
Charlotte played better with him starting last season. In a stretch where he played about 28 minutes a game, the team had the top offensive rating and the fifth-best defensive rating.
He is a late flyer outside the top 100, around round 10 or 11. The rookie center threatens his role, and he is not a long-term answer as the starter. The extra competition caps his upside.
Josh would take him over Ryan Kalkbrenner about 90 times out of 100 because Diabaté has the starting job. Josh still thinks Kalkbrenner would produce more if both played the same minutes.
A Yahoo ADP of 99 against an expert rank of 177 was called far too high.
One expert is not confident that he can keep up his shot blocking.
Charlotte plays 4-3-4 games in our playoff weeks and has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Charlotte has a deep roster and projects as a play-in team.

durable.text: He is an undersized center who cannot really protect the rim.
He is a good defender and hustle player who switches onto ball handlers and gets steals. He is one of the best offensive rebounders in the league.
He is getting better as a passer on short rolls.
He won the Hustle Player of the Year award.
He makes no threes. His fantasy value comes from FG% and rebounds.

note: Diabaté is on the edge of our 144-player pool. Yahoo ranks him 144 and ESPN 160, both value him at 0 to 0.2 USD, and he was not drafted last season. That makes him a 1 USD end-of-draft flyer for teams that want FG% (61.6% projected) and rebounds (8.0) from a starting center and do not need threes, though his FT% (65.2%) is a small drag. Early in the season, check whether he keeps the starting job and his 26 minutes a game against the rookie center and Kalkbrenner. If his minutes drop, he goes back to waivers.
